vegetation: Open black-spruce peat-plateau forest; evergreen shrubs, feather moss and lichens beneath the trees.
observed_composition: Euskirchen et al. (2014) report approximately 20% tree cover at the permafrost forest. Evergreen-shrub understory includes Rhododendron groenlandicum, Vaccinium vitis-idaea and Oxycoccus microcarpus. Ground layer is dominated by lichens and feather moss. Exact remaining PFT cover values were not transcribed from Figure 3.
observed_pft_summary: Needleleaf evergreen tree cover about 20%, plus evergreen shrubs and nonvascular ground cover; overlapping strata prevent complementing tree cover to bare ground.
denominator: Point-intercept cover: species hit at least once / all sampling points; multilayer total may exceed 100%. Four 100 m cardinal transects with points every 2 m.
observation_period: Study 2010–2013; exact vegetation-sampling date not specified in the read Methods.
spatial_scope: Permafrost-forest tower at the APEX peat-plateau site, corresponding to US-BZS; tower footprints of the three ecosystem sites reported distinct.
bare_ground: Not quantified; 80% non-tree area is not 80% bare soil.
source_title: AmeriFlux US-BZS; Euskirchen et al. 2014, Differential response of carbon fluxes to climate in three peatland ecosystems that vary in the presence and stability of permafrost
source_locator: Official site Overview; paper Sections 2.3 and 3.1, Figure 3.
verification_status: Official search-index overview and primary full text read on 2026-10-26; exact Figure 3 bar heights not digitized.
candidate_pft: Qualitative candidate: boreal needleleaf evergreen trees + broadleaf evergreen shrubs; preserve moss/lichen as separate nonvascular cover.
candidate_basis: Species physiology and measured partial tree cover; no closed 100% FATES vector established.
uncertainties: ENF metadata is compatible with an open peatland tree canopy and cannot establish 100% tree PFT. Vertical cover overlap and nonvascular representation matter.
next_evidence: Retrieve Figure 3 source data/BADM vegetation cover and inventory sampling date; reconcile with the active FATES parameter set.
functional_group_percent_basis: Point-intercept cover: species hit at least once / all sampling points; multilayer total may exceed 100%. vegetation: Groundwater-accessing velvet mesquite (Prosopis velutina) woodland with rain-responsive understory, notably big sacaton (Sporobolus wrightii), herbs and shrubs.
observed_composition: USGS SIR2005-5163 reports mesquite canopy fraction 0.74 for Charleston in 2001–2003, estimated from high-resolution aerial photographs within 100 m of tower. Lee et al. (2021) separately describe approximately 80% total vegetation cover; this is not an exclusive tree/grass partition.
observed_pft_summary: Broadleaf deciduous mesquite canopy 74% (historical horizontal crown cover); understory includes C4 bunchgrass but its area fraction is not reported in the passages read.
denominator: Mesquite crown projection / ground area within 100 m of flux tower; total vegetation estimate in Lee2021 uses another description and must not be subtracted directly.
observation_period: 2001–2003 mesquite cover; Lee2021 describes study with simulations/field observations in 2016–2017.
spatial_scope: Charleston mesquite site on the San Pedro River alluvial terrace; not Lewis Springs mesquite site or the separate sacaton grassland.
bare_ground: Not determined. The 26% outside mesquite crowns includes understory/litter and cannot be called bare ground.
source_title: AmeriFlux US-CMW; USGS Scientific Investigations Report 2005-5163, Chapter D; Lee et al. 2021, Convergent Hydraulic Redistribution and Groundwater Access Supported Facilitative Dependency Between Trees and Grasses in a Semi-Arid Environment
source_locator: Official Overview; USGS p.123, canopy-fraction table and accompanying aerial-photography paragraph; Lee2021 Section 2 and Table 1.
verification_status: Official indexed overview read; USGS primary indexed text p.123 read (direct PDF returned 403); Lee2021 full text read.
candidate_pft: Qualitative candidate: temperate/dryland broadleaf deciduous tree + C4 grass + other understory; exact FATES vector unresolved.
candidate_basis: Measured crown cover and species, preserving canopy/understory overlap.
uncertainties: 74% mesquite crown cover is not 74% of stems, basal area, or normalized vegetation-only PFT. Groundwater supply is critical to representation.
next_evidence: Retrieve BADM/field quadrat understory cover with seasonal date and an explicit canopy/ground-cover convention.
functional_group_percent_basis: Mesquite crown projection / ground area within 100 m of flux tower; total vegetation estimate in Lee2021 uses another description and must not be subtracted directly. | 2001–2003 mesquite cover; Lee2021 describes study with simulations/field observations in 2016–2017. | Charleston mesquite site on the San Pedro River alluvial terrace; not Lewis Springs mesquite site or the separate sacaton grassland.

site_name: Eight Mile Lake Permafrost thaw gradient, Healy Alaska
vegetation: Moist acidic tussock tundra dominated by Eriophorum vaginatum and Vaccinium uliginosum; deciduous/evergreen dwarf shrubs and moss/lichen ground layer.
observed_composition: Primary site description identifies Eriophorum vaginatum sedges; Vaccinium uliginosum, Rubus chamaemorus, Betula nana and Ledum palustre shrubs; Sphagnum, Dicranum, feather moss and lichens. No tower-footprint numerical functional fractions were verified in the sources read.
observed_pft_summary: C3 sedge/graminoid + deciduous and evergreen shrubs + nonvascular vegetation; OSH is not a shrub-only numerical fraction.
observation_period: Belshe2012 landscape study; Schuur laboratory site description; current AmeriFlux metadata checked 2026-10-26.
spatial_scope: Eight Mile Lake moist tundra/permafrost-thaw gradient; broader watershed land-cover classes are not the tower footprint.
source_title: AmeriFlux US-EML; Schuur Lab Eight Mile Lake; Belshe et al. 2012, Incorporating spatial heterogeneity created by permafrost thaw into a landscape carbon estimate
source_locator: Official Overview; PI laboratory site vegetation paragraph; Belshe2012 Section 2.1.
verification_status: Official indexed metadata, PI website and primary journal site description read.
candidate_pft: Qualitative candidate: arctic C3 graminoid/sedge + boreal deciduous and evergreen shrubs; retain moss/lichen separately.
candidate_basis: Observed species/growth forms only; no exact numeric vector.
uncertainties: Thaw gradient shifts from sedge toward shrub communities; watershed spatial heterogeneity and sampling year must be matched before deriving fractions.
next_evidence: Use footprint-matched BADM or point-intercept plots; Belshe2012 mapped land-cover and subsequent EML vegetation datasets are evidence leads, not borrowed tower fractions.
functional_group_percent_basis: No verified fractional denominator. | Belshe2012 landscape study; Schuur laboratory site description; current AmeriFlux metadata checked 2026-10-26. | Eight Mile Lake moist tundra/permafrost-thaw gradient; broader watershed land-cover classes are not the tower footprint.

vegetation: High-elevation Engelmann spruce/subalpine fir forest substantially disturbed by spruce beetle.
observed_composition: Frank et al. (2014) Section 2.1: Picea engelmannii 72% of stems and 84% of basal area; Abies lasiocarpa constitutes the remainder (derived 28% stems, 16% basal area). AmeriFlux reports outbreak peaking in 2008 with mortality of 85% of forested basal area.
observed_pft_summary: The reported two-species tree inventory comprises evergreen needleleaf taxa. This establishes tree functional identity, while vegetation/ground area and living fractions remain separate.
denominator: Tree stems and tree basal area; not horizontal land cover. Composition inventory cited to Speckman manuscript in preparation in Frank2014.
observation_period: Historical stand context in 2014 paper; exact species inventory date not stated in Section 2.1. Beetle outbreak peaked in 2008.
spatial_scope: GLEES AmeriFlux forest near 41°21.992′N,106°14.397′W; not the whole Medicine Bow National Forest.
bare_ground: Not quantified; 85% basal-area mortality is not 85% bare ground.
source_title: AmeriFlux US-GLE; Frank et al. 2014, Ecosystem CO2/H2O fluxes are explained by hydraulically limited gas exchange during tree mortality from spruce bark beetles
source_locator: Official Overview disturbance paragraph; Frank2014 Section 2.1.
verification_status: Official overview and primary journal indexed methods read; USDA primary PDF indexed with matching text.
candidate_pft: Needleleaf evergreen trees dominate historical tree population; no areal 100% vector approved.
candidate_basis: Both named overstory species map to needleleaf evergreen. Time-varying live/dead stand structure must accompany the mapping.
uncertainties: Historical composition cannot be applied as a living-canopy fraction after beetle mortality; inventory timing and canopy recovery unresolved.
next_evidence: Obtain dated live/dead spruce/fir census, understory regrowth and ground-cover observations through the modeled years.
functional_group_percent_basis: Tree stems and tree basal area; not horizontal land cover. Composition inventory cited to Speckman manuscript in preparation in Frank2014. | Historical stand context in 2014 paper; exact species inventory date not stated in Section 2.1. Beetle outbreak peaked in 2008. | GLEES AmeriFlux forest near 41°21.992′N,106°14.397′W; not the whole Medicine Bow National Forest.

vegetation: Mixed temperate forest dominated by red oak/red maple with hemlock and pine components.
observed_composition: Richardson et al. (2009) report basal-area percentages: red oak 36, red maple 22, other hardwoods 14, eastern hemlock 13, red pine 8, white pine 6. Rounded sum 99%. Thus reported broadleaf deciduous groups total 72% and needleleaf evergreen groups 27%.
observed_pft_summary: Historical measured basal-area grouping: BDT 72%, NET 27%, 1% rounding/unallocated; this is not a crown-cover vector.
denominator: Basal area of the historical EMS stand; primary paper rounded species/group percentages.
observation_period: Historical site composition quoted in 2009 paper; exact inventory date not specified there. Paper uses Harvard fluxes 1992–2004.
spatial_scope: Harvard EMS tower, distinct from Harvard hemlock (US-Ha2), Little Prospect Hill and the harvested Simes Lot.
bare_ground: Not quantified; basal-area shares carry no bare-soil information.
source_title: AmeriFlux US-Ha1; Richardson et al. 2009, Influence of spring phenology on seasonal and annual carbon balance in two contrasting New England forests; HF069 v47 Biomass Inventories at Harvard Forest EMS Tower since 1993
source_locator: Official Overview; Richardson2009 p.322 Study sites; HF069 Methods Trees and tables hf069-09, hf069-12.
verification_status: Primary PDF p.322 read. HF069 metadata and latest hf069-12 CSV through 2024 retrieved; latest calculation not adopted pending temporal/live-tree aggregation audit.
candidate_pft: Provisional historical basal-area proxy: BDT 72/99=72.73%, NET 27/99=27.27% of reported tree basal area; explicit normalization, not measured land-cover fractions.
candidate_basis: Sum six rounded published groups, then normalize their sum of 99 for a tree-competition proxy only.
uncertainties: Rounded historical values; canopy footprint and species composition change. Latest HF069 summary values require checking against live-tree date-resolved hf069-09 before use.
next_evidence: Recompute yearly live-tree basal-area shares from HF069 using the 34 EMS plots, excluding A4/A5/B5/G3/H3/H4 and all harvest plots; preserve DBH≥10 cm threshold and plot/date selection.
functional_group_percent_basis: Basal area of the historical EMS stand; primary paper rounded species/group percentages. | Historical site composition quoted in 2009 paper; exact inventory date not specified there. Paper uses Harvard fluxes 1992–2004. | Harvard EMS tower, distinct from Harvard hemlock (US-Ha2), Little Prospect Hill and the harvested Simes Lot.

vegetation: Spruce-hemlock dominated temperate/boreal transitional forest with other conifers and a hardwood minority.
observed_composition: Richardson et al. (2009) report basal area: Picea rubens 44%, Tsuga canadensis 26%, other conifers 21%, hardwoods 8% (chiefly Acer rubrum and Betula papyrifera). Rounded sum 99%; conifer groups total 91%.
observed_pft_summary: Historical tree basal area: NET 91%, BDT 8%, 1% rounded/unallocated.
denominator: Historical stand tree basal area; rounded species/group proportions, not land area.
observation_period: Historical composition attributed to Hollinger1999; restated 2009. Main-tower flux study uses 1996–2004.
spatial_scope: Main Howland research tower; do not copy into west or harvested tower as exact tower-specific vector.
source_title: AmeriFlux US-Ho1; Richardson et al. 2009, Influence of spring phenology on seasonal and annual carbon balance in two contrasting New England forests; Hollinger et al. 2004, Spatial and temporal variability in forest–atmosphere CO2 exchange
source_locator: Official site identifier; Richardson2009 p.322 Study sites; Hollinger2004 Methods p.1690 and Results p.1692.
verification_status: Primary PDF text read; official site metadata retrieved via official search listing.
candidate_pft: Provisional historical tree basal-area proxy NET 91/99=91.92%, BDT 8/99=8.08%; no ground-area claim.
candidate_basis: Functional grouping of historical conifer and hardwood percentages, normalized only across the reported 99%.
uncertainties: Historical rounded inventory and source location coordinates in 2009 prose are coarse. Later composition/canopy mortality may differ.
next_evidence: Extract dated main-tower live basal-area inventory and footprint weighting; compare with Hollinger2021 long-term measurements.

vegetation: Closed spruce-hemlock forest with fir, cedar, white pine, maple and birch.
observed_composition: Hollinger et al. (2004) sampled 48 plots around each main/west tower. Pooled descriptive groups: spruce + hemlock about 69% live basal area; maple + birch + white pine together 17%; remaining basal area mostly northern white cedar. West-tower total live basal area 56.7±16.5 m²/ha.
observed_pft_summary: Evergreen conifer majority demonstrated, but the 17% mixed conifer/hardwood group prevents an exact west-tower NET/BDT split.
denominator: Live tree basal area; composition is described jointly for two tower plot populations, not a separately tabulated Ho2 PFT partition.
observation_period: Historical 2004 publication; exact inventory date not explicit in the read vegetation methods.
spatial_scope: 48 circular plots per tower, radius 7.315 m, at 50/100/200/400 m along 30-degree azimuths; main and west towers separated ~775 m.
source_title: AmeriFlux FLUXNET US-Ho2; Hollinger et al. 2004, Spatial and temporal variability in forest–atmosphere CO2 exchange
source_locator: Official DOI dataset description; Hollinger2004 pp.1690 and 1692.
verification_status: Official DOI description and primary PDF methods/results read.
candidate_pft: Qualitative candidate: NET dominant + BDT minority; exact fractions unresolved.
candidate_basis: Direct local tree inventory groups; no transfer of main-tower 91:8 as a west-tower measurement.
uncertainties: Pooled composition and a mixed 17% group cannot supply two exclusive PFT fractions. Absolute west BA is not a PFT fraction.
next_evidence: Obtain Ho2 species-resolved live inventory, survey year and tower-specific plot-weighted composition.

vegetation: Spruce-hemlock forest subject to shelterwood harvest, with other conifers and hardwoods.
observed_composition: Official metadata calls the site a closed conifer forest. The site-listed Scott et al. (2004) harvest study reports preharvest basal area about 30 m²/ha and removal just under 30% of aboveground biomass. No verified postharvest numerical PFT composition was found.
observed_pft_summary: Needleleaf evergreen majority qualitatively supported; disturbance amount is not a PFT partition.
denominator: Absolute preharvest stand basal area and fraction of biomass removed, not species percentages or land-cover area.
observation_period: Shelterwood harvest 2001–2002; Scott2004 initial postharvest report; current site metadata checked 2026-10-26.
spatial_scope: Harvest tower and managed stand; distinct from the main and west unmanaged tower areas.
bare_ground: Not quantified; 30% biomass removal cannot be treated as 30% bare soil.
source_title: AmeriFlux US-Ho3; Scott et al. 2004, Changes in carbon storage and net carbon exchange one year after an initial shelterwood harvest at Howland Forest, ME
source_locator: Official Overview and listed publication; USDA primary publication abstract.
verification_status: Official metadata and USDA primary abstract read; exact species-level harvest/postharvest inventory not obtained.
candidate_pft: Qualitative candidate NET dominant + BDT minority with explicit disturbance history; no exact vector.
candidate_basis: Local published stand description and harvest metadata only.
uncertainties: AmeriFlux generic 'minimal disturbance' description conflicts with harvest designation/history; pre/post harvest and regrowth must be handled separately.
next_evidence: Retrieve Scott2004 species-resolved pre/post inventories and recent Ho3 BADM; retain harvest years in initialization/management metadata.
functional_group_percent_basis: Absolute preharvest stand basal area and fraction of biomass removed, not species percentages or land-cover area. | Shelterwood harvest 2001–2002; Scott2004 initial postharvest report; current site metadata checked 2026-10-26. | Harvest tower and managed stand; distinct from the main and west unmanaged tower areas.

vegetation: Dry ridge heath tundra with dwarf evergreen/deciduous shrubs, lichen and sedges; surroundings include extensive tussock tundra.
observed_composition: Cristóbal et al. (2017) report vegetation communities around the Heath tower as 20% heath, 72% tussock tundra, with the remaining 8% jointly sedge meadow and bare soil (8% derived complement). Species-level primary description identifies Dryas integrifolia, Carex, dwarf shrubs and lichens.
observed_pft_summary: Numerical community-patch mixture, not a direct shrub/graminoid PFT split. Both heath and tussock communities contain multiple growth forms.
denominator: Area proportions of vegetation community types around tower; mapping radius/precise footprint weighting not specified in the read paragraph.
observation_period: 2008–2012 study period; underlying community-map date not explicit in quoted description.
spatial_scope: Heath/Ridge tower near 68.607 N,149.296 W; not the full Imnavait catchment and not the Tussock tower.
bare_ground: Included with sedge meadow in the 8% remainder; separate bare-soil fraction unresolved (cannot assign all 8% to bare ground).
source_title: AmeriFlux US-ICh; Cristóbal et al. 2017, Estimation of surface energy fluxes in the Arctic tundra using the remote sensing thermal-based Two-Source Energy Balance model; Zona et al. 2023, Pan-Arctic soil moisture control on tundra carbon sequestration and plant productivity
source_locator: Official Overview; Cristóbal2017 Section 4.1 pp.1344–1345, especially p.1345; Zona2023 Section 2.1.
verification_status: Official indexed overview and primary HESS PDF text read; Zona primary full-text species paragraph read.
candidate_pft: Qualitative candidate arctic evergreen + deciduous shrubs, C3 sedge/graminoids and moss/lichen; include spatial mixing sensitivity.
candidate_basis: Verified patch mixture plus species/growth forms; no conversion of 20% heath into 20% shrubs.
uncertainties: Published CAVM class/table can mislabel Heath as G4, while PI-informed text calls it dry heath. Patch proportions and functional cover require reconciliation; nonvascular cover overlaps vascular canopy.
next_evidence: Obtain tower-specific point-intercept PFT cover and original community map, including separate sedge-meadow and bare-soil areas and footprint weights.

observed_composition: Cristóbal et al. (2017) report 95% tussock-tundra vegetation community around the Tussock tower. The remaining 5% is not classified in the read paragraph. Species composition within the community is qualitative, not 95% sedge.
observed_pft_summary: C3 sedge/graminoids + deciduous/evergreen dwarf shrubs + moss; 95% describes community area rather than a single PFT.
denominator: Area proportion of vegetation community type around the Tussock tower, not a sedge-only or vegetation-only PFT denominator.
observation_period: 2008–2012 study period; exact mapping date not stated.
bare_ground: Not quantified; unclassified 5% cannot be assigned to bare ground.
